To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of fixed length vectors is a bottleneck in the current encoder decoder architecture, 2) we can overcome this by introducing soft alignments, and 3) this results in an approach for neural machine translation that is competitive with the current state of the art.

we propose a novel approach to the problem of neural machine translation that allows the model to automatically ( soft )search for relevant parts of the source sentence, and we show that the proposed model achieves a translation performance comparable with the existing state of art.
we propose a new neural machine translation model, and that the proposed model performs comparably with the existing state of art phrase based system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the translation performance by making the search for relevant parts of the source sentence implicit.

extending the encoder decoder framework for neural machine translation by allowing the model to automatically ( soft )search for relevant parts of the source sentence that are needed to produce a target word.
improving the translation performance of neural machine translation models by introducing a soft alignment model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our proposed model, with its ability to automatically search for relevant parts of the input sentence, is able to achieve a translation performance that is comparable to the existing phrase based systems.
the new approach is a significant improvement over the existing state of art neural machine translation systems.

our proposed model is able to achieve a performance comparable to the state of the art statistical phrase based approach, without requiring explicit alignment information and hard to learn phrase tables, and while using a much simpler translation model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new approach that allows a model to automatically search for the relevant parts of a source text that are useful to predict the next word in a translation.

we have proposed an extension to the basic encoder decoder architecture for neural machine translation, and the extension allows a model to learn to (soft )align source words to target words during training, without requiring explicit segmentation.

, by jointly learning to align and translate, we can construct a neural machine translation model that is able to automatically discover the relevant parts of a source sentences for predicting a target word conditioned on the source context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the encoder-decoder framework can be extended with a soft alignment mechanism that can learn to search for the relevant parts of a source sentences without having to hardcode the alignment procedure.
it is possible to build a single neural network for machine translation, that can jointly learn to align and translate.
the encoder decoder architecture can be extended in a simple manner to allow the model to jointly learn to align and translate, and that such models can be useful in practice.
